scope: Primary-source audit for a ROCK1/ROCK2 structure-affinity baseline; no upstream code, GPU work, credentials, outreach or bulk provider download.

sources.title: Identification of Selective Dual ROCK1 and ROCK2 Inhibitors Using Structure-Based Drug Design
findings: The paper reports a hit-to-lead medicinal chemistry series intended to produce dual ROCK1/ROCK2 inhibitors, with enzyme, cell and in vivo assays.

The publisher table's rendered unit is µM (the low-resolution text rendering can appear as mM); independent ChEMBL records for the same paper store equivalent values in nM, for example 3.8 µM as 3800 nM and 2 nM as 0.002 µM. Preserve the original unit and convert only with an explicit unit field.

The paper reports cocrystal structures for an early lead in ROCK1, ROCK2 and PKA; the RCSB related entries are 6E99, 6E9L, 6E9W and 6ED6. RCSB 6ED6 specifically contains ROCK2 bound to compound 12 (ligand J0P).

The article's table includes weak controls and censored upper bounds. For example, compound 22 is reported as >10 µM for both ROCK1 and ROCK2; this is an experimentally assayed right-censored weak/inactive observation, not an exact inactive affinity. Compound 11 is weak in ROCK1 (15.81 µM) and ROCK2 (3.79 µM).

Compound 16 is reported as a potent dual inhibitor (table value approximately 0.017 µM ROCK1 and 0.002 µM ROCK2 in the accessible table); compound 58 is also reported with measured enzyme values (approximately 0.122 µM and 0.014 µM). These are measured enzyme endpoints, not binding Kd values.

assay_and_endpoint.target: ROCK1 and ROCK2 kinase enzyme assays; PKA and pMYPT1 are separate selectivity/cellular endpoints
assay_and_endpoint.endpoint: enzyme IC50 (half-maximal inhibition), with >10 µM censoring in some table cells
assay_and_endpoint.units: µM in the publisher table; equivalent ChEMBL records may be represented in nM; convert only after recording the original unit and censoring flag
assay_and_endpoint.negative_control_status: weak/inactive observations are assay-derived IC50 or >10 µM bounds, not decoys

sources.availability: Paper, ACS table and supporting information are publicly discoverable; ligand/protein coordinate files for deposited complexes are available through RCSB PDB.

findings: Human ROCK2 kinase construct, no listed mutation, X-ray structure at 2.86 Å; ligand J0P is N-[(2,3-dihydro-1,4-benzodioxin-5-yl)methyl]-4-(pyridin-4-yl)benzamide (the paper’s compound 12).

RCSB provides coordinate, sequence, ligand and validation data. The structure establishes a solved protein-ligand pose, but RCSB does not itself provide an affinity endpoint for this entry; link affinity to the paper’s assay table by compound identity and preserve that mapping as provenance.
This is a measured active complex, not an inactive control. A pose-only structure must not be treated as evidence that docking score or contact recovery predicts IC50.
Human ROCK2, no listed mutation, X-ray structure at 2.70 Å, ligand YEI/GNS-2664; the RCSB entry states the associated literature is to be published.

The coordinate and validation files are publicly available from RCSB, but this record alone supplies no published measured IC50/Kd and should be marked structure-only until an authoritative assay source is linked.
Do not use 8X8Z as a labelled positive affinity datum or infer an inactive control from the absence of an assay value.

sources.title: A versatile polypharmacology platform promotes cytoprotection and viability of human pluripotent and differentiated cells
findings: CEPT uses Chroman 1 (50 nM), emricasan (5 µM), polyamine supplement and trans-ISRIB (0.7 µM); Y-27632 is a comparator/recovery ROCK inhibitor in the biological experiments.

CEPT and Y-27632 effects are cellular recovery/viability or function endpoints. The same study also reports independent HotSpot kinase assays: Chroman 1 IC50 = 52 pM at ROCK1 and 1 pM at ROCK2, versus Y-27632 71 nM and 46 nM, respectively. These are experimentally measured component/comparator potencies, not an affinity label for the CEPT mixture; emricasan, polyamine and trans-ISRIB are not thereby assigned ROCK affinities.
Chromane/Y-27632 comparator performance must not be interpreted as a measured ROCK2 affinity control without a separate biochemical source.

benchmark_data_policy.label_definition: Primary label should be target-specific enzyme IC50 with original unit, assay format, construct, ATP/substrate context where available, censoring and source identifier retained. Kd/Ki/IC50 are distinct endpoints and must not be pooled as interchangeable.
benchmark_data_policy.positive_controls: Use structure-linked compounds only when the ligand identity in the PDB can be reconciled to the paper or an authoritative assay record. 6ED6/compound 12 is a suitable active structure-affinity anchor; 8X8Z is structure-only pending an assay source.
benchmark_data_policy.inactive_controls: Use measured weak compounds or right-censored >10 µM observations as assay controls with censoring flags. Do not call random docking decoys, untested library molecules, or missing affinity records inactive.
benchmark_data_policy.rock1_rock2: Keep ROCK1 and ROCK2 as separate target labels or a multi-task target field. Dual inhibition cannot be represented by a single potency number without a prespecified aggregation rule.
benchmark_data_policy.cept: Keep CEPT as a separate biological-use track. It is a four-component post-thaw intervention and cannot be predicted by a ROCK affinity model as a mixture or as equivalent to Y-27632.

leakage_risks: The ACS series is a congeneric medicinal chemistry campaign; random molecule splits can put near-identical analogues in train and test and substantially overstate generalisation.
Several PDB entries and assay rows refer to the same compound series. Any structure-affinity benchmark must group exact compounds, salt forms, stereoisomers and close analogue series across folds.
RCSB structures are selected for crystallisation and are not a random sample of assay compounds; structure availability is a selection variable and must not be treated as independent test evidence.

ChEMBL ROCK records can combine IC50, Ki, Kd, activity assay formats, constructs and units across laboratories. Deduplicate by canonical ligand and assay metadata, preserve censored values, and split by scaffold/series and publication source.
A structure-only entry such as 8X8Z has no negative label. Missing affinity must remain missing/withheld rather than being converted to inactivity.
strict_validation_requirements: Create a source-linked table with target isoform, ligand identifier/SMILES, PDB ID, assay endpoint, unit, numeric value or censoring bound, construct and publication DOI.

Hold out complete medicinal chemistry series and any ligand with a solved structure from model development when testing prospective structure transfer; report a separate structure-only pose-recovery analysis.
Use an external assay source or a new blinded biochemical batch for validation. Do not count CEPT cell viability or Y-27632 cellular comparator data as enzyme-affinity validation.
Report ROCK1 and ROCK2 performance separately, with weak/inactive controls explicitly identified as measured, censored or untested.
decision: 6ED6 plus the 2018 ACS assay table is a defensible primary structure-affinity anchor for ROCK2 and a dual-ROCK medicinal chemistry series, provided IC50 units and censoring are preserved. 8X8Z is publicly available structural context but currently lacks a primary published affinity label. CEPT supports biological relevance only; it is not an affinity-model training or negative-control source.
